title: Which journeys do ST-BO04 and ST-BO05 time?
description: Each measure is a duration (from a supersession until every affected service is named and regenerated; from an agent's first declaration to an accepted one), so under Lathe 5 each times a journey, and lathe check warns outcome-duration-without-journey for both. I propose two journeys. For ST-BO04, Fix reaches every service: trigger, a component digest or runtime version is superseded; steps, ST-DIS-UC04 Ship a component fix without a compiler release, ST-DIS-UC05 Learn that a pinned component is superseded, ST-DIS-UC02 Find every service built from a component, ST-GEN-UC03 Take a component fix into a service; result, every affected service regenerated with the successor before the fail date. For ST-BO05, Agent reaches an accepted declaration: trigger, an agent gets a service goal; steps, ST-DECL-UC01 Start a service declaration, ST-DECL-UC03 Check a declaration, ST-DECL-UC04 Repair a refused declaration, ST-EXT-UC02 Qualify a fill; result, an accepted declaration with qualified fills. Each journey serves its outcome and has one journey test. The upgrade wrote no journey.

title: Which other outcomes does a journey reach, and in what order of work?
description: Lathe 5 adds journeys to Discovery: a journey strings use cases and handoffs, in order, from a trigger to a result that a business outcome measures, and serves that outcome as a capability does. The upgrade wrote none. Apart from ST-BO04 and ST-BO05 (ST-Q03), I propose a journey only where an outcome's result needs several use cases in order: ST-BO02 Consumers feed the registry (ST-SUP-UC02 Compose a registry for a team, ST-SUP-UC06 Contribute a component upstream, ST-SUP-UC05 Graduate or retire a component) and ST-BO06 Golden paths stay safe (ST-SUP-UC04 Introduce an experimental component, ST-SUP-UC05 Graduate or retire a component, ST-SUP-UC10 Curate a golden path with its default concerns). ST-BO01, ST-BO03, ST-BO07, ST-BO08 and ST-BO09 are measured by a sweep or a study at one moment and need no journey now. The journeys come after the decisions on the essential and accidental classes, so that their steps carry out use cases that are stable.

title: Through which CLI command or CLI query does the command line reach the 19 commands and queries it does not reach now?
description: After the CLI split (D2), lathe check warns step-unreached for 88 flow steps: they invoke one of 19 commands or queries that no CLI command or CLI query sits under, and ST-IF01 (Command line) offers their use cases. The old cli_command records had no record for them, so this is a design gap, not a lost record. For each, the options are: add a CLI command or CLI query under it with its usage (and a CLI handler for its file); make the steps variants of another interface; or stop offering the use case through ST-IF01. The commands and queries: ST-DIS-CMD08, ST-DIS-QRY03, ST-DLV-CMD01, ST-DLV-CMD02, ST-DLV-CMD03, ST-DLV-CMD04, ST-GEN-CMD05, ST-SUP-CMD01, ST-SUP-CMD02, ST-SUP-CMD03, ST-SUP-CMD04, ST-SUP-CMD05, ST-SUP-CMD06, ST-SUP-CMD07, ST-SUP-CMD08, ST-SUP-CMD09, ST-SUP-CMD10, ST-SUP-CMD11, ST-SUP-QRY03.

title: How does ST-ASR-SP06 come to say that a CLI handler is read as a handler?
description: Q07 (decided 2026-11-02) adds to ST-STD-CODE-R01 and R02 that a CLI handler is a code-titled record, which is done, and asks ST-ASR-SP06 to say that a CLI handler is read as a handler. SP06 is an essential specification, and Lathe refuses every write to it: its statement names Lathe, a table, an entry point and a generator, because its subject is the technical kinds, as the essential review found (the owner left SP05 and SP06 as they are). Options: A, retire SP05 and SP06 and let the rule tests of ST-STD-CODE-R01 and R02 carry their predicates, as the review proposed; B, split each into an essential sentence the product's people own and a predicate the rule test owns; C, leave SP06 as it is, with R02 saying it. The code already reads a CLI handler as a handler.
